successCriteria.description: verifyToken resolves to a principal { userId: string; role: string } for a JWT signed with the process.env JWT_SECRET, and rejects (typed error) for invalid, expired, or tampered tokens.
extractTokenFromHeader returns the token string for a well-formed "Bearer <token>" Authorization header and returns null for undefined, empty, non-Bearer-scheme, or malformed headers.
The authenticate preHandler attaches request.user = { userId, role } after successful JWT verification and rejects the request with a 401-mapped error when the token is missing or invalid.
requireRole(...roles) returns a preHandler that allows the request when request.user.role is among the supplied roles and rejects with a 403-mapped error otherwise.
The Fastify request type augmentation compiles under strict TypeScript so that downstream code accessing request.user.userId and request.user.role type-checks without casts.
The barrel export re-exports all public auth symbols so consumers import exclusively from the shared auth entry point.
JWT_SECRET is read from process.env at verification time and is never hardcoded anywhere in source or tests.

constraints: No `any` type — use `unknown` with type guards for the decoded JWT payload (HARNESS no-any, high severity).
JWT_SECRET must never be hardcoded or logged; read it from process.env (HARNESS no-hardcoded-secrets, critical; GP-004 no sensitive data in logs).
RBAC is enforced in middleware, never inline in route handlers or business logic (GP-005; AGENTS.md architecture rule 4).
All async paths in the preHandler hooks must catch errors and convert them to Fastify reply errors — no unhandled promise rejections (GP-006).
Auth/RBAC failures must throw the existing UnauthorizedError (401) and ForbiddenError (403) from src/shared/errorTypes.ts rather than introducing new error classes.
The phase must not add new runtime dependencies — jsonwebtoken and @types/jsonwebtoken are already declared in package.json.
Code must compile under the existing strict tsconfig.json (strict null checks, no implicit any) and pass the Jest verification command.
outOfScope: JWT token signing/issuance and the /auth login endpoint — this phase only verifies tokens; issuance is a separate auth phase.
Registering the authenticate/requireRole hooks on any leave routes — that is Phase 8 (leave routes and app registration).
OIDC/corporate identity provider integration — production identity wiring is out of scope; this phase provides the local JWT verification primitives.
Refresh-token handling, token rotation, and session TTL enforcement (HARNESS identity.sessionTtlMinutes) — not part of this utility phase.
User lookup or role resolution from a database — the principal { userId, role } comes solely from the verified JWT claims.

ambiguities.description: The intent says "Read JWT_SECRET from process.env" but does not specify behavior when JWT_SECRET is unset/empty at verification time.
options: Fail fast at module load with a clear configuration error (refuse to start)
Reject each verifyToken call with UnauthorizedError at runtime
Treat empty secret as a configuration bug and throw a typed error only when verification is attempted

entityInvariants.invariant: A successfully verified principal always carries a non-empty userId and a non-empty role string; verification never yields a principal with missing or empty identity fields.
request.user is set only after the authenticate preHandler has successfully verified a valid JWT; downstream handlers may rely on request.user being present only on routes where authenticate has run.
A role guard permits the request if and only if request.user.role is a member of the supplied role set; it never mutates request.user and never permits when request.user is absent.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth required to call; this is the primitive that establishes identity.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects with a typed error (UnauthorizedError) for invalid, expired, or signature-mismatched tokens; never returns a partial or null principal on success.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Pure function, no auth side effects.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null for any malformed/missing header rather than throwing; never throws on bad input.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Must run before any protected route handler; on success attaches request.user so subsequent handlers and role guards can read identity.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Missing or invalid token → 401 (UnauthorizedError); all async errors caught and surfaced as Fastify reply errors (GP-006).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Must be chained after authenticate so request.user is populated; checks request.user.role membership in the supplied set.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Role not in set or request.user absent → 403 (ForbiddenError); never throws an unhandled rejection.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Auth/RBAC failure errors must be the existing UnauthorizedError and ForbiddenError classes so the controller error-mapping (401/403) stays consistent.
JWT_SECRET must be read from process.env following the same direct-env-read pattern used for DATABASE_URL and NODE_ENV.

The request.user shape ({ userId: string; role: string }) must match exactly what Phase 7 controllers and Phase 8 routes will read (request.user.userId, request.user.role) so the type augmentation is the single source of truth.
Unit tests must live under tests/unit/shared/auth/ and match the Jest testMatch glob (**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)) and ts-jest transform already configured.
The barrel export must follow the existing shared-module export convention (re-export public symbols from the package entry point) as established by src/modules/leave/index.ts.

integrationPoints.why: verifyToken delegates signature verification and claim decoding to this library; no alternative crypto implementation should be introduced.
authenticate and requireRole must be usable as Fastify preHandler hooks so Phase 8 can register them on protected routes.
Downstream consumer that will register authenticate on all leave routes and requireRole('manager','admin') on approve/reject/pending endpoints.
Downstream consumer that reads request.user.userId as employeeId/reviewerId; depends on the type augmentation making those fields typed.
Reuses UnauthorizedError and ForbiddenError for auth/RBAC failures so error mapping stays consistent across the codebase.
